newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia gives Yuganskneftegaz July tax pay deadline.
newsitem.headline: Russia gives Yuganskneftegaz July tax pay deadline.

text.p: The Russian tax service could seize property of oil company Yuganskneftegaz if it does not pay tax arrears by July 1, a State Tax Service bulletin distributed at a briefing on Wednesday said.

The bulletin quoted tax service head Alexander Pochinok as ordering a regional tax authority to take action if the company did not fully pay its debt, which as of May 1 was 2.6 trillion roubles ($445.7 million).

"In the case of non-payment, or partial payment of arrears on current payments, take measures determined by law to penalise the property of Yuganskneftegaz, firstly on securities which are the property of the given enterprise," the bulletin said.

The tax service said Yuganskneftegaz, the main production unit of a financial group controlled by Bank Menatep, owns a $35.0 million stake in Tokobank, while it deposited $6.8 million with Vneshtorgbank in 1995 for Ministry of Finance bonds.

The chairman of Rosprom-YUKOS, the Menatep group, Mikhail Khodorkovsky said at the end of May that Yuganskneftegaz planned to issue bonds to cover the amount of the debt under a government scheme to restructure enterprise debt.

The plan allows companies to issue securities covering the debt which would then be held by the government as collateral against payment. In case of a default on payments, the government could sell the securities.
Khodorkovsky said the same scheme would be applied to another Rosprom-YUKOS subsidiary, Samaraneftegaz.

The State Tax Service said the net debt to the federal government of all the subsidiaries of YUKOS, an oil holding company within the Rosprom-YUKOS group, had doubled in the year to May 1 to 4.25 trillion roubles.
YUKOS owed a total of 6.68 trillion roubles, including fines, on May 1, the tax service said.
